The annotated candidate has been saved verbatim to `answer.json`.

The solution preserves every original C token and the original `//@ assert(i != j);` assertion, adding only:
- A function contract `requires x >= 0;` (supports termination for the loop variant)
- A single grouped `/*@ ... */` block on the `while` loop containing:
  - `loop invariant x >= 0;`
  - `loop invariant y - x == j - i;` (the key invariant that connects `y`, `i`, and `j`)
  - `loop assigns x, y;`
  - `loop variant x;`

Reasoning: `i` is the original `x` and `j` the original `y`. Invariant `y - x == j - i` holds initially (both sides 0) and is preserved since both `x` and `y` decrement together. At loop exit `x == 0`, so `y == j - i`. Inside `if (y != 0)` we get `j - i != 0`, hence `i != j`, which proves the original assertion. No admit/assume/axiom was used and no C tokens were changed.
